metadata.title: qfim-bench: reproducible benchmarking of Grover-based quantum frequent itemset mining
metadata.description:
qfim-bench 1.1.0

Reproducible benchmarking of Grover-based frequent itemset search on simulators and IBM Quantum hardware. This software does not demonstrate quantum advantage. The marked set is computed classically, and the method is a one-shot Grover search over all 2^n itemsets, not level-wise Apriori.

What changed since v1.0.1

  • Corrected circuit. Matched diffusion operator (diffusion="matched"|"hadamard"); the earlier flat curve for the ansatz start came from a mismatched Hadamard diffusion. Item-to-qubit ordering fixed, with asymmetric end-to-end tests.
  • Marking. Data-driven marked sets by default; cardinality and explicit sets still available. Three oracle styles (mcx, mcz, mcx_vchain); mcz needs about half the two-qubit gates.
  • Statistics. Wilson and Clopper-Pearson intervals, TVD null-floor calibration with permutation p-values, fidelity-decay fit, trivial baselines, unknown-M tools.
  • Guarded hardware backend. Write-once manifest, job cap, shot count and usage budget from the manifest, per-job time limit, multi-circuit jobs, billed-seconds recording, SHA-256 manifest hash in the runners.
  • Hardware results. Preregistered ladder on ibm_marrakesh (n = 3, 4, 5, M/N = 1/8, 5 runs each, one sitting, one calibration window): amplification works at n=3 (0.796 at r=2 vs 0.124 at r=0), still works narrowly at n=4 (0.568), and is gone at n=5 (0.194). Raw counts, manifests and analysis are in results/hardware/ and campaigns/. The simulator is 0.04 to 0.14 above the hardware at r = 1, 2.
  • Packaging. Pinned lock file, Dockerfile, CONTRIBUTING.md, CI for Python 3.10-3.13 on Linux, macOS and Windows. 184 tests pass (90% line coverage in a clean environment).
  • Dashboard. New hardware-ladder tab with ideal curve, prediction bands and the single-calibration-window limit.

Limits

One device, one calibration window, three sizes. FakeMarrakesh is a single calibration snapshot. The plan was committed and pushed before the runs but not git-tagged. See review/CLAIMS_MAP.md for what the results do and do not support.

Install

pip install -r requirements-lock.txt then pip install -e . --no-deps, or docker build -t qfim-bench .
